Practical information

Everything you need to plan your stay in Bilbao for AICES 2027, 4 to 7 May 2027.

The venueUniversity of Deusto

Founded in 1886 by the Society of Jesus, the University of Deusto is one of the oldest private universities in Spain, with campuses in Bilbao and San Sebastián.

The Bilbao campus sits on the right bank of the estuary, directly opposite the Guggenheim Museum and between the Guggenheim and the Euskalduna Conference Centre. Its oldest building, the classicist Main Building (1886), was designed by Francisco de Cubas.

The CRAI Library, designed by Rafael Moneo, is linked to the Main Building by the Pedro Arrupe footbridge, which also connects the campus with the city centre and the museum district.

Avenida de las Universidades 24, 48007 Bilbao

TravelGetting to Bilbao

Bilbao is well connected by air, rail and road. The airport is only about 20 minutes from the city centre.

By air: Bilbao Airport (BIO)

About 12 km north of the city and roughly 15 to 20 minutes by road. Airport information is on the Aena website.

Bilbao Airport (Aena)

Airport bus A3247 (Bizkaibus)

Runs between the airport and Bilbao Intermodal bus station, with city-centre stops on Gran Vía, Plaza Moyúa and Alameda Recalde, roughly every 15 to 20 minutes; the journey takes about 20 to 30 minutes. Single ticket 5 EUR on board (cheaper with a Barik travel card). Note: since October 2026 the Alameda Recalde stops are temporarily replaced by Puente de Deusto/Zubiarte because of a tunnel closure; check the Bizkaibus page before travelling.

Bizkaibus airport line Barik card fares

Taxi

Taxis wait outside arrivals. A ride to the city centre or to Deusto typically costs around 27 to 35 EUR, depending on time and traffic.

Other airports

Santander (about 1 hour by road) and Vitoria (about 45 to 60 minutes) are alternatives; both have coach connections to Bilbao Intermodal.

Bilbao Intermodal bus station

By train or coach

Long-distance Renfe trains arrive at Bilbao-Abando Indalecio Prieto station in the city centre (metro Abando). Intercity coaches use Bilbao Intermodal (metro San Mamés).

Renfe Bilbao Intermodal

Local transportGetting around

Metro Bilbao

Lines L1 and L2. Deusto and Moyua stations are both less than a 10-minute walk from campus; Abando, Casco Viejo and San Mamés serve the main hotel areas.

Metro Bilbao Map and frequencies

Tram (Euskotren)

The tram runs along the riverside through the museum district. From the Guggenheim stop, cross the Pedro Arrupe footbridge to campus.

Euskotren tram

City and regional buses

Bilbobus (city) and Bizkaibus (regional) stop near campus. One Barik card works on metro, tram, Bilbobus and Bizkaibus.

Bizkaibus Barik card

On foot

Most recommended hotels are within 5 to 30 minutes of campus on foot. The Deusto bridge and the Pedro Arrupe footbridge link the campus with the city centre.

Campus on Google Maps Virtual campus tour

AccommodationUniversity and student residences

Budget-friendly alternatives for students and early-career researchers. Availability for short stays must be requested directly.

Deusto Hall of Residence (Colegio Mayor Deusto)

University residence run by Deusto; accepts guests from other universities and shorter stays, subject to availability.

Website

Micampus Bilbao

Student residences in Bilbao; ask about short stays for event participants.

Website

RESA San Mamés

Website

The cityDiscover Bilbao

Bilbao, capital of Bizkaia in the Basque Country, was for more than a century one of the great industrial and shipbuilding centres of Europe. Since the 1990s it has reinvented itself around culture, design and services, a change often summed up as the "Guggenheim effect".

The city is compact and walkable: the Old Town, the 19th-century Ensanche, the riverside promenades and the Deusto campus are all within about 30 minutes on foot of each other, and the metro reaches the Atlantic beaches in roughly half an hour.

Guggenheim Museum Bilbao

Frank Gehry's titanium-clad museum (1997), right across the river from campus.

More information

Old Town and the Seven Streets

Medieval core of the city, full of pintxo bars, small shops and the Santiago Cathedral.

More information

La Ribera Market

Riverside food market in the Old Town, one of the largest covered markets in Europe.

More information

Bilbao Fine Arts Museum

Major collection from the Middle Ages to contemporary art, a short walk from campus.

More information

Bizkaia Bridge

The world's oldest transporter bridge (1893), a UNESCO World Heritage Site, reachable by metro.

More information

San Juan de Gaztelugatxe

Hermitage on a rocky islet on the Bizkaia coast, about 45 minutes by road; access may require prior booking in busy periods.

More information

Good to knowPractical tips

Weather in May
Mild and changeable, typically around 12 to 20 C, with a real chance of rain. Bring a light jacket and an umbrella.
Languages
Basque (Euskara) and Spanish are both official; English is widely understood in hotels and at the venue.
Currency and payments
Euro (EUR). Contactless card payment is accepted almost everywhere.
Electricity
230 V, 50 Hz, European two-pin plugs (types C and F).
Emergencies
Call 112 for any emergency service (police, ambulance, fire).
Time zone
Central European Summer Time (UTC+2) in May.
Visa
Check whether you need a Schengen visa well in advance; see the AICES visa page. AICES visa page
Tourist information
Bilbao-Bizkaia Tourist Office, Plaza Circular 1, next to Abando station.
